acceptance: A journey test with the real logged-out output of the CLI reports the logout, not a quota wall
The signal test reads the exact text, with the /login step
A real quota wall still reports quota
An empty review report names the cause
fix: Classify an authentication failure apart from a quota wall, from what the CLI prints and from the usage probe. Emit a code that names the logout and the next step: run /login, then evolve clihealth clear claude. A review run with an empty report states that the run did not complete.
summary: Near 01:00 on 2026-11-05 the claude CLI was logged out. Lanes then reported a quota wall with stop_reason quota-pause, at 56 percent weekly usage, and the loop stopped for six hours. Reviews returned an empty report and an empty verdict. The operator requires that each signal states the true cause and a next step that works. This signal states a false cause, and its next step is to wait for a reset that will not help. A known memory entry records this confusion from earlier incidents.
title: A logged-out CLI must not be reported as a quota wall
